note: A recorded session of real MCP tool calls against Remedy's own server (/api/mcp, streamable HTTP), written by scripts/public/record-mcp-session.mjs. These are the tool calls an AI assistant makes to help an owner, from the recall to a claim ready to pay; no AI model was called to record them, and the photo was answered by the verification cache, the model's recorded answers replayed. {origin} is the server's own address. Demonstration in PayPal sandbox; Brightline Home and its recall are fictional.
owner: I got a recall notice for my Brightline laptop charger. What do I do?

steps.why: Find the recall from the owner's own words.
steps.text:
3 recalls for "Brightline 65W laptop charger" (elastic search):
1. Recall BH-2026-01, 2026-10-15: Brightline Home recalls 65W laptop chargers (sample recall). Photo refund: Cut the cord, $34.99 refund. {origin}/recalls/BH-2026-01
2. Recall FW-2026-01, 2026-10-29: Fernway Home recalls 65W laptop chargers (sample recall). Photo refund: Cut the cord, $29.99 refund. {origin}/recalls/FW-2026-01
3. Recall 25248, 2025-05-01: Baseus Portable Chargers Recalled Due to Fire Hazard; Sold on Amazon.com by Shenzhen Baseus Technology. Remedy: Replace. {origin}/recalls/25248

steps.why: Read what the recall asks the owner to do and photograph.
steps.text:
Recall BH-2026-01: Brightline Home recalls 65W laptop chargers (sample recall).
It pays on a photo. First: Cut the cord. Remedy: Full refund of $34.99.
Steps: Unplug the charger. Cut the cord where it meets the charger case. Take one photo of the cut cord with the charger.
Official remedy: "Stop using the charger and cut the power cord where it meets the charger case. Send one photo of the cut cord with the charger for a full refund of $34.99."
Source: stored rule, none (written by the sample firm). Details: {origin}/recalls/BH-2026-01

steps.why: Give the owner their own claim link and checklist. Nothing is opened yet.
steps.text: To claim the refund for recall BH-2026-01 (Brightline Home recalls 65W laptop chargers (sample recall)), the owner opens {origin}/claim/BH-2026-01, follows these steps: Unplug the charger. Cut the cord where it meets the charger case. Take one photo of the cut cord with the charger., and takes one photo. They choose where the refund goes. Demonstration in PayPal sandbox; Remedy is not affiliated with the recalling firm.

steps.why: The owner has cut the cord and taken one photo. Check it before anything is opened: verify_photo stores nothing and pays nothing, and this photo was checked before, so the verification cache answers with no model call.
steps.text:
Verified.
C1 Right product: unclear. We could not confirm this is the exact recalled product.
C2 Made safe: pass. The photo shows the product made safe.
C3 Your own photo: pass. This is a new photo of the product.
C4 Within the recall: pass. No model or lot number is needed for this recall.
C5 Claim limits: pass. This claim is within the limit for one purchase.
C6 Not already refunded: pass. No PayPal purchase linked.
Without an API key only the free checks run: photo quality and the own-photo match. A photo checked before is answered from the verification cache, with no model call. Add a key for the full checks.

steps.why: The photo checks out: open the claim with it, which runs the six checks again on the server's own record.
